summary: Track 31 (Config-Driven Audit-as-Code Profiles) — DONE. Verdict: PROTOTYPE FIRST, novelty Low-Moderate, scope ADDITIVE. Design: versioned YAML/JSON audit-profile schema in front of existing cli.py flags — profile_id/extends/regulatory_mapping/metrics(core+extended+active)/subgroups/statistics(alpha, bootstrap_resamples, n_min_guard)/drift_monitoring/overrides[]/ci_cd. Guard-safety: tightening NFR-001(alpha)/NFR-002(bootstrap floor)/NFR-003(n>=30) never needs approval; loosening any of them requires an overrides[] entry (nfr_id, justification, approved_by) plus an auto-stamped append-only audit-overrides.log line — enforced by a profile_validator.py module importable by both cli.py (run-time) and Track 32's CI (commit-time gate). Metric-pool separation enforced at validator level so extended/plugin metrics (Track 29 registry.py) always render regulatory-unmapped even when the profile's top-level regulatory_mapping is set (Track 36 requirement). metrics.active is the reserved metric-selection field Track 29 asked for. drift_monitoring block is optional/orthogonal to Track 21's Layer-2 CUSUM. Two examples provided (EU-AI-Act-default.yaml baseline; client-strict-v1.yaml extending + tightening it, no override needed since tightening only). Open decisions flagged, not resolved: exact schema.py Core Four enum values, NFR-001's exact bound direction/NFR-002's exact floor (only current operating defaults α=0.05/B>=1000 were available from team memory, not the source NFR doc text), and whether an override on NFR-003 should still respect a hard absolute floor. Research-only, no repo/code edits. Full report: results/31_audit_as_code_profiles.md (delivered as file, not committed to repo).
